Header.CaseTitle: Sterling Investments Ltd v Blackwood Capital Partners LLP
Header.AppealFrom: High Court of Justice, King's Bench Division

Counsel.Lead: Sarah Moore KC; Elizabeth Edwards (instructed by Freshfields Bruckhaus Deringer LLP)

SummaryOfPosition.Summary: The Respondent denies breach of duty and contends that the investment decisions complained of fell within the scope of its contractual discretion and were reasonable in the market conditions prevailing at the material time.

FactsReliedOn.item: The Investment Management Agreement granted the Respondent broad discretionary powers over investment decisions.
The technology investments were made following detailed analysis and were consistent with the Appellant's stated risk appetite.
Market conditions in 2019-2020 were unprecedented and the losses were attributable to unforeseeable market events.
The Respondent provided quarterly reports in accordance with contractual requirements.
The portfolio's performance was consistent with comparable funds in the same period.

Contentions.item: The investment decisions fell within the scope of the discretion granted by the Agreement.
The Respondent exercised reasonable skill and care in the prevailing market conditions.
The losses were caused by unprecedented market volatility, not any breach of duty.
The Appellant accepted the risk of loss when entering into a discretionary investment arrangement.

LegalBasis.item: Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, s.138D
